steps: Line a tray with baking parchment. For the fudge, combine the condensed milk and 100g of the caster sugar in a pan over low-medium heat. Stir constantly to stop the milk solids from burning at the bottom; some golden flecks are fine. Cook for 7-10 mins still stirring, until very thick. Pour onto the lined tray, leave to cool completely, then cut into small-ish chunks.

For the cookie dough, brown the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat, swirling occasionally, until deeply golden and nutty. Remove from the heat and immediately add half of the Ceylon tea. Leave to steep for 6-8 mins, then strain through a fine sieve, pressing gently on the leaves. Leave to cool until just warm but still fluid.
Meanwhile, toast the milk powder in a dry frying pan over low heat, stirring constantly, until lightly golden and nutty, about 8-10 mins. Transfer to a bowl and leave to cool completely.

Grind the remaining tea in a spice or coffee grinder or a high-powered mini food processor. Mix the flour with 3g of the finely ground tea, the bicarbonate of soda and a pinch of salt in a large bowl.

In a separate bowl, beat the warm infused butter with both sugars until smooth and glossy. Beat in the whole egg and yolk until fully combined, then mix in the condensed milk and vanilla extract. Add the dry ingredients and mix just until incorporated. Fold through the condensed milk fudge pieces. Leave the dough to rest at room temperature for 20-30 mins.

Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4 and line a large baking tray with baking parchment. Mix the remaining caster sugar with the last of the finely ground tea in a small bowl. Divide the dough into 12 portions of around 70–75g each. Roll lightly into balls, finally shaping them so they're slightly taller than they are wide. Then roll each ball in the sugar mixture to coat. Bake in two batches, spacing the cookies well apart and lightly pressing the tops first to encourage them to spread. Sprinkle the flaky sea salt over, if you like.

Bake for 10-12 mins, turning the tray halfway through until the edges are set and golden but the centres remain soft and slightly pale. They will look underdone in the middle, which is correct for a chewy finish. Remove from the oven and leave to cool on the tray for 5 mins before transferring to a wire rack. The cookies will settle and firm slightly as they cool, while remaining thin and bendy in the centre.
